title: Enterprise Integration Platform Architecture
content:
# Enterprise Integration Platform Architecture
Document ID: ARC-001

The fictional Acme Enterprise integration estate uses multiple integration technologies. Boomi supports SaaS/application and batch integrations. Axway API Gateway exposes selected partner and external APIs. Layer7 API Gateway protects internal and customer-facing APIs with authentication and policy enforcement. SFTP supports legacy partner file exchange. Integration services depend on identity providers, databases, ERP/CRM platforms and downstream microservices.

title: Enterprise Integration Platform Architecture
content: Troubleshooting must follow the transaction across layers. A gateway error does not automatically mean the gateway is the root cause.

title: Middleware Platform Support Overview
content:
# Middleware Platform Support Overview
Document ID: ARC-003

Integration Operations provides L2/L3 operational support for Boomi runtimes and processes, Axway and Layer7 API gateways, SFTP flows and common integration dependencies. Application owners retain ownership of business application defects; infrastructure, network, database and IAM teams own their respective platforms. P1 incidents use a coordinated major-incident bridge.

title: Payment Integration Flow
content:
# Payment Integration Flow
Document ID: ARC-002
Service: PaymentService

title: Payment Integration Flow
content:
Client -> Axway API Gateway -> Payment Integration Service -> Payment Backend -> Payment Database

Authentication occurs at the API edge. Axway performs routing and policy enforcement. The Payment Integration Service transforms and validates the request before invoking the backend.

title: Payment Integration Flow
content: 401 normally requires authentication/policy investigation. 504 requires latency/dependency tracing. A database bottleneck can manifest to the client as a gateway 504.

title: INC001 - Boomi Order Integration Failure
content:
# INC001 - Boomi Order Integration Failure
Incident: INC001
Severity: P1
Platform: Boomi
Service: OrderIntegration

title: INC001 - Boomi Order Integration Failure
content: Production order messages stopped reaching ERP after a connection component was changed during a release.

title: INC001 - Boomi Order Integration Failure
content: Boomi runtime was healthy. Process Reporting showed authentication failures against the ERP endpoint. The deployment contained an incorrect production credential reference.

title: INC001 - Boomi Order Integration Failure
content: The team rolled back the connection component to the last known-good packaged component, validated one order transaction, and then released queued processing.

title: INC001 - Boomi Order Integration Failure
content: Runtime health alone does not prove end-to-end integration health. Deployment and connection-component versions must be correlated during triage.

title: INC002 - Layer7 Authentication Outage After Certificate Rotation
content:
# INC002 - Layer7 Authentication Outage After Certificate Rotation
Incident: INC002
Severity: P1
Platform: Layer7
Service: CustomerAPI

title: INC002 - Layer7 Authentication Outage After Certificate Rotation
content: CustomerAPI returned HTTP 401 shortly after the identity provider rotated its signing certificate.

title: INC002 - Layer7 Authentication Outage After Certificate Rotation
content: Layer7 token validation was using stale signing-key/trust information.

title: INC002 - Layer7 Authentication Outage After Certificate Rotation
content: The approved signing-key/trust configuration was refreshed and authentication tests passed.

title: INC002 - Layer7 Authentication Outage After Certificate Rotation
content: For sudden widespread 401 responses, compare IdP key/certificate changes before assuming client credentials are incorrect.

title: INC003 - Payment API HTTP 504
content:
# INC003 - Payment API HTTP 504
Incident: INC003
Severity: P1
Platform: Axway
Service: PaymentService

title: INC003 - Payment API HTTP 504
content: Payment API calls through Axway returned intermittent 504 responses.

title: INC003 - Payment API HTTP 504
content: Gateway nodes were healthy. Network connectivity succeeded, but backend response time increased beyond the gateway timeout. The payment backend was waiting on an exhausted database connection pool.

title: INC003 - Payment API HTTP 504
content: Database slowness caused backend requests to exceed the API gateway timeout.

title: INC003 - Payment API HTTP 504
content: Database blocking activity was resolved and the application connection pool recovered. Gateway timeout was not increased.

title: INC003 - Payment API HTTP 504
content: A gateway 504 can be a downstream symptom. Trace the complete dependency chain before modifying gateway timeouts.

title: INC004 - Integration Database Connectivity Degradation
content:
# INC004 - Integration Database Connectivity Degradation
Incident: INC004
Severity: P2
Service: CustomerSync

title: INC004 - Integration Database Connectivity Degradation
content: Customer synchronization showed intermittent database connection-acquisition timeouts.

title: INC004 - Integration Database Connectivity Degradation
content: A long-running reporting query consumed database resources and caused application connection pools to queue.

title: INC004 - Integration Database Connectivity Degradation
content: The database team terminated the problematic workload and tuned the query. Integration latency returned to baseline.

title: INC005 - Partner SFTP Transfer Failure
content:
# INC005 - Partner SFTP Transfer Failure
Incident: INC005
Severity: P2
Service: PartnerFileExchange

title: INC005 - Partner SFTP Transfer Failure
content: Outbound partner files failed after the partner rebuilt its SFTP server.

title: INC005 - Partner SFTP Transfer Failure
content: The partner host key changed. The integration correctly rejected the untrusted fingerprint.

title: INC005 - Partner SFTP Transfer Failure
content: The new fingerprint was independently verified through the approved partner-security process and then updated under change control.

title: INC005 - Partner SFTP Transfer Failure
content: Never bypass host-key validation merely to restore service.

title: Production Change and Emergency Change Policy
content:
# Production Change and Emergency Change Policy
Document ID: POL-CHG-001

All production middleware changes require traceability and authorization. Standard changes follow normal approval. Emergency changes must still document risk, implementation, validation and rollback. Direct unrecorded configuration edits are prohibited. Incident pressure does not remove the need for change traceability.

title: P1 Major Incident Escalation Policy
content:
# P1 Major Incident Escalation Policy
Document ID: POL-P1-001

Declare P1 when a critical production service has severe business impact, widespread transaction failure or no acceptable workaround. Start the major-incident bridge, assign technical and incident leads, preserve correlation IDs/log evidence, engage required platform/dependency owners, communicate at agreed intervals and maintain a timeline. Restoration is prioritized over speculative root-cause changes; RCA follows stabilization.

title: Middleware Certificate Rotation Procedure
content:
# Middleware Certificate Rotation Procedure
Document ID: SOP-CERT-001

Maintain certificate owner, purpose, endpoints and expiry metadata. Test the new certificate and chain in non-production. For production rotation, back up configuration, implement through change control, validate TLS/authentication end-to-end and monitor errors after change. Never copy private keys into tickets, source control or RAG knowledge documents.

title: Integration Platform Disaster Recovery Procedure
content:
# Integration Platform Disaster Recovery Procedure
Document ID: SOP-DR-001

DR invocation requires an authorized decision according to business-impact criteria. Confirm primary-site impairment, identify affected critical services, activate the documented secondary runtime/gateway components, validate secrets/certificates/connectivity, and perform end-to-end business validation. Record recovery time and data/replay considerations. Failback must be planned and controlled rather than automatic.

title: Daily Middleware Health Check
content:
# Daily Middleware Health Check
Document ID: SOP-OPS-001

Review Boomi runtime/process health, Axway and Layer7 node status, API error/latency trends, certificate-expiry alerts, SFTP queue/failure status, critical dependency health and unresolved P1/P2 incidents. Health checks should include business-flow validation rather than platform-up status alone.

title: Middleware Production Deployment Procedure
content:
# Middleware Production Deployment Procedure
Document ID: SOP-DEPLOY-001

Production changes require approved change records, implementation plan, validation plan and rollback plan. Capture current versions before deployment. After deployment, validate platform health plus at least one representative end-to-end transaction. If critical failures begin immediately after deployment and rollback criteria are met, prefer the approved rollback over ad-hoc production modifications.

title: Generic API 5xx Troubleshooting Runbook
content:
# Generic API 5xx Troubleshooting Runbook
Document ID: RB-API-001

title: Generic API 5xx Troubleshooting Runbook
content: Capture correlation ID and timestamp; identify which layer produced the 5xx; trace client -> gateway -> integration runtime -> backend -> database/dependency; compare error rate and latency with baseline; check deployments and infrastructure events; inspect a representative transaction end-to-end; and search known-error and historical-incident records before changing production configuration.

title: Axway Backend Connectivity Failure
content:
# Axway Backend Connectivity Failure
Document ID: RB-AXWAY-002
Platform: Axway API Gateway

title: Axway Backend Connectivity Failure
content: Connection refused, connection reset, DNS failure, TLS handshake error or intermittent backend connection errors.

title: Axway Backend Connectivity Failure
content: Validate backend hostname and port, DNS resolution, route/firewall path, TLS certificate chain, truststore, supported protocol/cipher configuration and backend listener health. Compare the failing node with another gateway node to isolate node-specific configuration.

title: Axway Backend Connectivity Failure
content: Restore the dependency or configuration, then execute a controlled API request and confirm gateway and backend logs share the same correlation ID.

title: Axway API Gateway HTTP 504 Runbook
content:
# Axway API Gateway HTTP 504 Runbook
Document ID: RB-AXWAY-001
Platform: Axway API Gateway

title: Axway API Gateway HTTP 504 Runbook
content: HTTP 504 generally indicates that the gateway did not receive a timely response from an upstream or downstream dependency.

title: Axway API Gateway HTTP 504 Runbook
content:
1. Capture API name, gateway node, correlation ID, backend endpoint and timestamp.
2. Confirm whether the 504 is generated by Axway or another intermediary.
3. Test backend connectivity from the gateway network.
4. Check DNS resolution, routing, firewall and TLS handshake.
5. Compare backend response time with configured gateway timeout.
6. Review recent policy, routing or backend URL changes.
7. Check backend health, thread/connection pools and database dependencies.
8. Search historical incidents for the same API and dependency.
9. Do not simply increase timeout until the slow dependency is understood.

title: Axway API Gateway HTTP 504 Runbook
content: Escalate to the backend owner when the gateway is healthy but the backend is slow or unavailable. Engage network/security teams for connectivity or TLS failures.

title: Boomi Atom or Molecule Unavailable Runbook
content:
# Boomi Atom or Molecule Unavailable Runbook
Document ID: RB-BOOMI-002
Platform: Boomi

title: Boomi Atom or Molecule Unavailable Runbook
content: Scheduled processes do not start, executions remain queued, or the runtime appears offline.

title: Boomi Atom or Molecule Unavailable Runbook
content:
1. Confirm runtime status in Boomi platform.
2. For Molecule deployments, determine whether one node or the complete cluster is affected.
3. Check host availability, CPU, memory, disk space and filesystem access.
4. Review runtime/container logs around the failure timestamp.
5. Validate outbound connectivity required by the runtime.
6. Confirm certificates and proxy configuration have not changed.
7. Restart a runtime only under the approved operational procedure.
8. For a multi-node Molecule, prefer controlled failover over restarting all nodes simultaneously.

title: Boomi Atom or Molecule Unavailable Runbook
content: After recovery, execute a health-check process and validate one end-to-end business transaction before releasing queued traffic.

title: Boomi Production Process Failure Runbook
content:
# Boomi Production Process Failure Runbook
Document ID: RB-BOOMI-001
Platform: Boomi
Environment: PROD
Owner: Integration Operations

title: Boomi Production Process Failure Runbook
content: Troubleshoot a Boomi integration process that fails repeatedly in production.

title: Boomi Production Process Failure Runbook
content:
- Process executions move to Error state.
- Documents are not delivered to the target application.
- Retry count increases.
- Business transactions remain pending.

title: Boomi Production Process Failure Runbook
content:
1. Confirm the affected process, Atom/Molecule, environment, execution ID and failure start time.
2. Review Process Reporting and capture the first meaningful connector or process error.
3. Verify whether the Atom or Molecule nodes are online and healthy.
4. Check recent deployment/package changes for the affected process.
5. Validate source and target connectivity independently.
6. Check credentials, certificates, API tokens and connection-component changes.
7. Inspect document-level errors and determine whether failures affect all messages or specific payloads.
8. Validate disk, memory and runtime resource health where applicable.
9. Retry one controlled transaction only after the suspected dependency is healthy.
10. If failures continue, stop uncontrolled retries and escalate with execution IDs and evidence.

title: Boomi Production Process Failure Runbook
content: Treat as P1 when a production critical business flow is unavailable with no workaround.

title: Boomi Production Process Failure Runbook
content: Attach execution ID, process name, Atom/Molecule name, error message, timestamps, deployment version and affected transaction count.

title: Middleware Certificate Expiry Runbook
content:
# Middleware Certificate Expiry Runbook
Document ID: RB-CERT-001

title: Middleware Certificate Expiry Runbook
content: TLS handshake failures, PKIX/trust errors, API authentication failures or sudden connectivity loss around a certificate expiry/rotation.

title: Middleware Certificate Expiry Runbook
content: Identify the certificate presented on the failing path, inspect expiry and chain, determine whether the issue concerns identity or trust, validate hostname/SAN, confirm intermediate certificates, and check relevant gateway/runtime truststores. Compare against recent certificate-change records.

title: Middleware Certificate Expiry Runbook
content: Monitor certificates before expiry, maintain ownership metadata and test rotations in non-production before production implementation.

title: Integration Database Connection Pool Exhaustion
content:
# Integration Database Connection Pool Exhaustion
Document ID: RB-DB-001

title: Integration Database Connection Pool Exhaustion
content: Connection acquisition timeout, increased integration latency, 5xx errors and queued transactions.

title: Integration Database Connection Pool Exhaustion
content: Measure active/idle/max connections, database availability, long-running queries, leaked connections and traffic spikes. Determine whether pool exhaustion is the cause or a symptom of database slowness. Do not increase pool limits without validating database capacity.

title: Integration Database Connection Pool Exhaustion
content: Resolve the underlying database/query issue, allow connections to recover, then validate integration latency and error rate.

title: Layer7 OAuth HTTP 401 Troubleshooting
content:
# Layer7 OAuth HTTP 401 Troubleshooting
Document ID: RB-L7-001
Platform: Broadcom Layer7 API Gateway

title: Layer7 OAuth HTTP 401 Troubleshooting
content: Clients receive HTTP 401 while the backend service may remain healthy.

title: Layer7 OAuth HTTP 401 Troubleshooting
content:
1. Determine whether rejection occurs at the gateway or backend.
2. Validate Authorization header presence and token format.
3. Check token expiration, issuer, audience and required scopes.
4. Validate OAuth/JWT verification policy and identity-provider availability.
5. Check signing certificate/JWK rotation and gateway trust configuration.
6. Review recent policy migrations or configuration changes.
7. Confirm clock synchronization when token time claims appear invalid.
8. Use a known-good token for a controlled test; never place production secrets in incident notes.

title: Layer7 OAuth HTTP 401 Troubleshooting
content: Expired token, incorrect audience/scope, rotated signing key, stale JWK cache, IdP outage, or an incorrect gateway policy.

title: Layer7 Gateway Policy Failure Runbook
content:
# Layer7 Gateway Policy Failure Runbook
Document ID: RB-L7-002
Platform: Broadcom Layer7 API Gateway

title: Layer7 Gateway Policy Failure Runbook
content: API returns unexpected 4xx/5xx responses after a policy deployment or migration.

title: Layer7 Gateway Policy Failure Runbook
content: Identify the policy revision, compare it with the last known-good version, inspect failed assertions, validate context variables and routing assertions, check referenced encapsulated assertions, certificates and cluster properties, and correlate gateway audit logs with the request ID. If the incident began immediately after an approved deployment, follow rollback criteria rather than making untracked production edits.

title: Enterprise SFTP Integration Failure
content:
# Enterprise SFTP Integration Failure
Document ID: RB-SFTP-001

title: Enterprise SFTP Integration Failure
content: File transfer fails, authentication is rejected, host key changes, connection times out or files remain unprocessed.

title: Enterprise SFTP Integration Failure
content: Confirm hostname/port, network reachability, service account status, SSH key validity, host-key fingerprint, remote directory permissions, filename convention, disk space and partner availability. A changed host key must be verified through an approved security channel before acceptance.

title: Enterprise SFTP Integration Failure
content: Retry a controlled file after the dependency is restored and confirm that duplicate-file protection prevents duplicate business processing.
